title: DR1 accepts document files up to 50MB; the frontend refuses anything over 10 MB.

finding.frontend: The file question's hint reads "Your file must be:" over the bullet "smaller than 10 MB", and the same 10 MB is enforced twice — in the browser, from the data-max-file-size attribute on the form, and on the server, where an oversize upload is answered with "The selected file must be smaller than 10 MB" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:40-52). The constant is deliberate rather than arbitrary: the comment above it records that 10 MB decimal was chosen to sit clear of the CDP nginx ingress cap of 10 MiB.
finding.prototype: DR1's file requirements list opens with "files that are smaller than 50MB" (app/views/upload-documents.html:165-170) — five times the frontend's ceiling, and the first thing the trader reads about their file.
finding.difference: Raise the accepted file size to 50MB, in the hint, in the client-side check and in the server-side limit, and restate the oversize error to match. This cannot land in the frontend alone: the current 10 MB exists to stay under the platform's 10 MiB ingress limit, so the ingress cap and the upload service's own limit have to be raised first or a 50MB file will be rejected by the platform before the application sees it. Confirm the real ceiling with the platform before changing the copy, because a hint promising 50MB over an ingress that refuses it is worse than the honest 10 MB.
finding.falsifiedBy: Uploading a file between 10 MB and 50MB through the frontend and having it accepted.

relatedTo.why: both rewrite the same four-line file requirements list
